title: Drawdowns, losing streaks and risk of ruin

inOneLine.simple: Losing runs happen to every trader. Deep falls are much harder to climb back from, so keep each loss small.
inOneLine.balanced: After a [[drawdown]] d, you need a gain of d ÷ (1 − d) to get back. [[losing-streak|Losing streaks]] are normal, and [[risk-of-ruin|risk of ruin]] rises fast as risk per trade grows.

explain.simple: A drawdown is how far your account has fallen from its highest point. Losses and gains are not equal: lose 50% and you need 100% just to get back. Losing streaks are normal, even for a plan that works over time. If you trade long enough, you will see one. Small risk per trade keeps a streak from becoming a disaster. Never raise size to win it back.
explain.balanced: Recovery needed = d ÷ (1 − d): 10% needs 11.1%, 20% needs 25%, 50% needs 100%. If each trade loses with chance L, independently, the chance that the next N trades all lose is L^N. The chance of seeing such a run somewhere in many trades is much higher. Risk of ruin is the chance of falling to a level where you must stop. It depends on win rate, reward to risk, risk per trade and your ruin level, and is best explored by simulation. Watch [[correlation]] too: two trades on pairs that move together can lose together, like one bigger trade.

assumptions: Example account with a peak of 10,000 USD
Drawdowns of 10%, 20% and 50% from that peak
steps: 10% drawdown: account at 9,000 USD. Gain needed = 0.10 ÷ 0.90 = 11.1%.
20% drawdown: account at 8,000 USD. Gain needed = 2,000 ÷ 8,000 = 0.20 ÷ 0.80 = 25%.
50% drawdown: account at 5,000 USD. Gain needed = 0.50 ÷ 0.50 = 100%.
The deeper the fall, the faster the climb back grows. Small losses keep you in the shallow part.

assumptions: Example loss chance per trade: 50%, and each trade is independent of the last
Example rule: 1% of current balance risked per trade, on a 10,000 USD account
Stops fill at their level, no costs
steps: Chance the next 5 trades all lose = 0.5^5 = 0.03125, about 3.1%.
Chance of at least one run of 5 losses somewhere in 100 trades is about 81%. Over many trades, a streak is likely.
5 losses at 1% each: 10,000 × 0.99^5 = 9,509.90 USD, a drawdown of about 4.9%.
That streak is unpleasant but survivable. The same streak at a much bigger risk per trade would be far deeper.

explainSimpler: Falling down a hole is quick. Climbing out takes longer the deeper it is. Expect losing runs, and keep each loss small so you never fall too far.
commonMistake: Thinking a losing streak means the plan is broken, or that a win is now 'due'. Each trade is a new event. The other big mistake is raising size to recover losses, which makes ruin more likely.

quickCheck.prompt: Your example account falls 30% from its peak. What gain do you need to get back?

options.explanation: No: the gain is measured on a smaller balance, so it must be bigger.
No: 0.30 ÷ (1 − 0.30) is about 42.9%, not double the drawdown.

quickCheck.prompt: You have had 6 losses in a row while following your plan. What is a sound response?

options.text: Double the size, because a win is due
options.explanation: No: a win is not due, and bigger size after losses deepens the drawdown.

options.text: Keep or cut the risk, pause, and review the trades against the plan
options.explanation: Right: streaks are normal. Review whether the rules were followed before changing anything.

options.text: Delete the losing journal entries so they do not drag down your statistics
options.explanation: No: losing trades are part of the honest record.

quickCheck.prompt: You buy EUR/USD and GBP/USD, each risking your example 1%. Why might your real risk be higher than 1%?

options.text: The pairs may move together, so both can lose at once
options.explanation: Right: correlated trades can act like one bigger trade, here up to about 2%.

options.text: It cannot: each trade is only 1%
options.explanation: No: two trades that each risk 1% can lose about 2% together.

doItNow.instructions: Open Learn → Calculators. In Losing streak chance, keep 100 trades and a 50% example loss chance, and try streaks of 5, 8 and 10. Then in Risk of ruin (simulated), compare risk per trade of 1%, 2% and 5% with the other inputs unchanged. Write down what you notice.

homework: Write one rule for what you will do after a losing streak, for example pause and review after a set number of losses. Add it in More → Risk rules.
